2. Mr Osman Ghani, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the allegations disclosed in the petition of complaint are civil in nature and in fact, for realisation of money of the petition of complaint, the opposite party No.2, that is, Agrani Bank, Rangpur Cadet College Branch, Rangpur by instituting Artha Rin Case No. 7 of 2002 got a decree for the said amount, as such the instant proceeding if allowed to continue that will perpetuate an injustice to the accused petitioner, as such, for ends of justice, the aforesaid case is liable to be quashed. 

 6. A proceeding can be quashed if on a reading of the complaint/FIR it appears that the allegations made in the petition of complaint/FIR does not in any way bring the accused petitioner within the ambit of the penal provision or the allegations made in the petition of complaint is  barred by law or if is of opinion of the Court that if the petition of complaint be allowed to continue that will not bring any fruitful result to the complainant or the informant. On a reading of the complaint it appears the offence/allegations made therein are relating to bank transaction and Government for realising of bank transaction or default made in the bank transaction, promulgated Artha Rin Adalat Ain. It appears from Annexure-C that on the self-same avennerits made in the petition of complaint, Bank filed Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 7 of 2002 and obtained a decree for the amount mentioned in the complaint. It also appears from paragraph 8 of the complaint that the Bank admitted that the accused petitioner has already made part payment of the said. Amount Annexure-F is the decree and we find the bank has already got the decree of the amount and put the decree into execution through Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Rangpur. On a perusal of the schedule of the complaint we find accused petitioner has mortgaged several acres of land to the Bank, In 1990 BLD (AD) 141 it has been held that.the allegations if it is found to be disclosed civil liabilities and for which, if the complainant initiated a suit before the appropriate Civil Court, the same allegations cannot be brought into Criminal proceeding. We find from the reading of the complaint and plaint of the suit that same allegations were before the criminal Court as well as before the civil Court, since there is a decree in civil Court as per decision of 14 DLR (SC) 14, 45 DLR (AD) 31 and 51 DLR (AD) 14, where the matter is in seisin of the Civil Court no criminal proceeding can be continued. We find substance in this Rule.
